title: Requests and company
intro: The last unit of A1 is about getting things done with other people: telling and asking someone to do something (*Gel!*, *Oturyň!*), asking them not to (*Gitme!*, *Gelmäň!*), saying who you are with and what something is for (*ejäm bilen*, *seniň üçin*), and joining words and sentences with *we, hem, ýöne, emma* and *ýa-da*.

blocks.text: To tell one person you know well to do something, use the bare stem of the verb, the infinitive without *-mak* or *-mek* ([A1 unit 6](a1-u06)): *gelmek* → *Gel!* (Come!), *okamak* → *Oka!* (Read!). To speak to several people, or politely to one, add `-(Y)ň`: *-yň, -iň* after a consonant, just *-ň* after a vowel: *Geliň!*, *Okaň!* This polite form is the one to use with anyone older or anyone you don't know well.

Three things in the table you have seen before. The ending follows vowel harmony and the rounding rule: *görüň*. A verb whose stem ends in *e* changes it to *ä* before *-ň*: *işle* → *işläň*, *diňle* → *diňläň*. And the verbs that soften *t* to *d* before a vowel do it here too: *gidiň*, *ediň*, *aýdyň*, *serediň*.
**Don't.** For **don't**, add *-ma* or *-me* to the stem: *Gelme!* (Don't come!), *Okama!* For the polite or plural form, *-maň* or *-mäň*, with *ä* after a front vowel: *Gelmäň!*, *Okamaň!*

**Please.** Add *haýyş edýärin* (please, literally **I request**) before or after the request: *Oturyň, haýyş edýärin.* When you offer something, invite someone in or hand something over, say *Buýruň!*: here you are, please, go ahead. You may also come across a longer polite form in *-ňyz* (*Geliňiz*), and friendly forms in *-sana* (*Okasana!*), which you will meet later.

blocks.title: ýapmak means to close
blocks.text: *ýap!* is **close!**: *Gapyny ýapyň* (Close the door), and **open** is *aç!*: *Gapyny açyň*. And *ýaz!* is **write!**, not spring.

**With** is *bilen*, a separate word that comes **after** its noun: *ejäm bilen* (with my mother), *Merdan bilen* (with Merdan). With a means of transport it is **by**: *awtobus bilen*, by bus; *uçar bilen*, by plane. Between two nouns it can also mean **and**: *Aýna bilen Merdan*, Aýna and Merdan.

Nouns stay as they are before *bilen*, but **me**, **you** and **him** or **her** are the genitive: *meniň bilen* (with me), *seniň bilen*, *onuň bilen*. With **us** and **you** (plural or polite) both *biziň bilen* and *biz bilen*, *siziň bilen* and *siz bilen* are written; **with them** is *olar bilen*. Ask **with whom?** with *kim bilen?*

items.en: I'm going to the market with my mother.
We're going to Mary by train.

blocks.title: A separate word
blocks.text: *bilen* is never written onto the word: *ejäm bilen*, not *ejämbilen*. And **me**, **you**, **him** take the genitive before it: *meniň bilen*, not *men bilen*.

**For** is *üçin*, which works like *bilen*: a separate word after its noun, with *meniň, seniň, onuň* before it (and *biziň* or *biz*, *siziň* or *siz*, *olar*). *Bu seniň üçin* (This is for you), *Türkmenistan üçin*, *ejäm üçin*. You already know it from *näme üçin?* (why?, literally **for what?**).

*şonuň üçin*, **for that**, is the everyday way to say **so** or **that's why**: *Men aç, şonuň üçin aşhana barýaryn.* (I'm hungry, so I'm going to the kitchen.) It answers *näme üçin?* the way *sebäbi* (because) does, from the other side.

items.en: I'm looking for a present for my father.

items.tk: Howa sowuk, şonuň üçin biz öýde.
items.seg: Howa sowuk, şonuň üçin biz öý|de.
items.en: The weather is cold, so we're at home.

blocks.title: sebäbi or şonuň üçin
blocks.text: Give the reason after *sebäbi*: *Biz öýde, sebäbi howa sowuk.* Give the result after *şonuň üçin*: *Howa sowuk, şonuň üçin biz öýde.* Both say the same thing.

You know *we* (and), *hem* (also; and) and *ýöne* (but) from [A1 unit 4](a1-u04). Two more: *emma*, also **but**, a little more formal and frequent in writing, and *ýa-da*, **or**, written with a hyphen.

items.en: Would you like tea or coffee?

items.tk: Men türkmençe biraz bilýärin, emma gowy gürlemeýärin.
items.seg: Men türkmençe biraz bil|ýär|in, emma gowy gürle|me|ýär|in.
items.en: I know a little Turkmen, but I don't speak it well.
Come tomorrow or the day after.

blocks.title: ýa-da in questions
blocks.text: In a choice question the particle *-mY* goes on the verb at the end, not on each choice: *Çaý ýa-da kofe isleýärsiňizmi?*

summary: To one friend, the bare stem: *Gel!*, *Oka!* To several people or politely, `-(Y)ň`: *Geliň!*, *Okaň!*, *işläň*, *gidiň*.
Soften a request with *haýyş edýärin*; offer with *Buýruň!*

*bilen* (with, by, and) and *üçin* (for) are separate words after the noun; **me, you, him** before them take the genitive: *meniň bilen*, *seniň üçin*; then *biziň* or *biz*, *siziň* or *siz*, and *olar bilen*.
*şonuň üçin* is **so, that's why**. *emma* is **but**, *ýa-da* is **or**.
